preparation.base: Python 3.10 conda environment (`osx-64` for `pyminimap2` SSE build, `minimap2 2.31`, `samtools 1.25`, `pip install .` from unmodified upstream v1.8.3 source)
preparation.without_preparation: Automated verification returned `undetermined` (`missing_file`) because the documented `nanoRepeat.py` command in `README.md` (lines 69-78) references an external GRCh37 archive (`NanoRepeat_v1.3_example_data/HG002/GRCh37_chr1.fasta`) that is not shipped in the repository and targets GRCh37 rather than `hg38`, so the automated profile stopped rather than rewriting undocumented paths.
steps: # On Linux x86_64 (use CONDA_SUBDIR=osx-64 on Apple Silicon for pyminimap2 SSE):
conda create -y -n nanorepeat -c conda-forge -c bioconda python=3.10 pip minimap2 samtools
conda activate nanorepeat && pip install NanoRepeat==1.8.3

recommendations: Provide a generic `hg38` CLI example in `README.md` (lines 69-78) with standard placeholder filenames (e.g. `input.bam`, `hg38.fa`, `regions.bed`) in addition to the downloadable GRCh37 archive so automated evaluators can run `nanoRepeat` directly against `hg38` datasets.

Use indexed FASTA access (`pysam.FastaFile`) instead of loading the entire reference genome into `ref_fasta_dict` in `src/NanoRepeat/nanoRepeat_bam.py` (line 710) and passing it to `multiprocessing.Process`, which consumes several GB of RAM and stalls under macOS `spawn` multiprocessing.

Replace `import distutils` in `src/NanoRepeat/tk.py` (lines 33-34) with `shutil.which` so NanoRepeat works on Python 3.12+, and allow using CLI `minimap2` without requiring `pyminimap2` SSE compilation on ARM64.

verdict.title: Runs in manual verification
verdict.reason: Installed unmodified upstream NanoRepeat v1.8.3 (`aa5ceb4`) into an isolated Python 3.10 environment (`pip install .`, zero source modifications) and ran `nanoRepeat` (`-t bam -d ont_q20 -c 4`, using standard Linux `fork` multiprocessing start method on macOS) against the 1000 Genomes ONT R10 SUP `hg38` CODIS reference slice (`ont-bam-hg38`, `HG00113`) with 4-column `regions.bed`. Execution completed in 24 seconds (exit 0), producing `HG00113.NanoRepeat_output.tsv` with 20/20 quantified forensic autosomal CODIS STR loci.

run.cmd: python3.10 -c "import multiprocessing, sys; multiprocessing.set_start_method('fork'); from NanoRepeat.nanoRepeat import main; sys.argv=['nanoRepeat','-i','/data/in/input.bam','-t','bam','-d','ont_q20','-r','/data/in/hg38.fa','-b','/data/in/regions.bed','-c','4','-o','/data/out/HG00113']; main()"

limitations: Results apply exclusively to the exact Git commit SHA and manually prepared environment recorded in this report.
Single regional reference slice per input type; low-coverage warnings on sliced BAMs do not imply defects on whole-genome data.
Plausible Output checks verify structural format and recognizable STR loci, not biological genotype truth.
Verification is a point-in-time snapshot; upstream repository changes after this commit are not covered until re-verification.
